papers.title: A single-channel EEG classification system for multiscale characterization of mouse vigilance state
papers.summary: This paper presents a single-channel EEG framework for classifying mouse sleep stages using a convolutional-recurrent classifier with causal temporal smoothing and hypnodensity analysis. It achieved 0.897 accuracy and 0.856 macro-F1 across unseen animals, preserving sleep architecture features and generalizing to long-term recordings.

papers.title: Day and night variation of plasma melatonin and glucocorticoids in a subterranean rodent endemic to north-west Argentina in two seasons.
papers.summary: This study measured day/night plasma melatonin and glucocorticoid profiles in wild tuco-tucos (Ctenomys coludo) during summer and winter, finding higher melatonin and cortisol during subjective night, consistent with nocturnal activity. Cortisol levels were 25-50 times higher than corticosterone.

papers.title: Rapid associative spine enlargement is required for cognitive function and stable wakefulness
papers.summary: The authors developed SynC, a chemogenetic tool that selectively blocks rapid associative spine enlargement in mouse neocortical neurons. Acute inhibition of spine enlargement impaired cognitive behaviors and reduced pairwise spike correlations during wakefulness, while sparing baseline firing and gamma activity, indicating that rapid spine enlargement is required for stable awake cognition.

papers.title: The Astrocyte Clock Controls Circadian Perineuronal Net Remodeling, Synapse Strength and Learning Behavior.
papers.summary: This study found that astrocyte-specific deletion of Bmal1 in mice reduces hippocampal perineuronal nets (PNNs) and abolishes their circadian rhythm, leading to increased synaptic strength but blunted long-term potentiation and impaired learning and memory. It suggests astrocyte circadian clock regulates PNN remodeling and plasticity.

papers.title: Chronic psychosocial stress: A primary driver of sleep apnea onset in rats and humans.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study combined rat experiments and Mendelian randomization in humans to show that chronic psychosocial stress (social isolation) is a primary driver of sleep apnea onset, increasing apneas and ventilatory responses in male rats. Human genetic analysis linked loneliness to sleep apnea risk independent of adiposity.

papers.title: Exercise and Circadian Rhythm Regulation: Mechanisms, Resilience, and Therapeutic Potential for Neurological Diseases.
papers.summary: This review summarizes mechanisms by which exercise modulates circadian rhythms, including clock gene regulation, hormonal/metabolic synchronization, and reduced neuroinflammation, and discusses therapeutic potential for stroke and Alzheimer's disease. Evidence suggests appropriately timed exercise may restore circadian alignment and improve neurological outcomes.

papers.title: Conditional Spatial Classification of Expert-Confirmed Interictal Epileptiform Discharge Epochs: An EEG-ECG Ablation and SHAP Analysis
papers.summary: This study developed a conditional spatial classifier to categorize expert-confirmed interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) epochs into five scalp distribution categories. Adding ECG channels improved test accuracy up to 94.44%, with SHAP analysis attributing about 31% of importance to ECG features, though this is model-specific and not evidence of physiological biomarkers.

papers.title: Early Ictal Dynamics in Childhood Absence Epilepsy: Scalp EEG Detection of Direct Current Shifts and High-Frequency Oscillations.
papers.summary: The paper reports two pediatric cases of childhood absence epilepsy where scalp wide-band EEG captured ictal direct current (DC) shifts and high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) within the same seizure epochs. A reproducible temporal sequence was observed: a negative DC shift emerged hundreds of milliseconds before the first spike-and-wave complex, followed by spike-locked HFOs, suggesting that scalp wide-band EEG may enable early ictal biomarkers.

papers.title: Clinical EEG In Modern Psychiatry: Diagnostics and Prediction.
papers.summary: This review discusses the role of clinical EEG in psychiatry, highlighting its utility in detecting epileptiform activity, excluding organic brain dysfunction, and monitoring treatments. It also summarizes evidence for quantitative EEG features, such as alpha peak frequency and frontal alpha asymmetry, in predicting treatment responses in depression, though with modest effect sizes.

papers.title: Single-channel gamma burst dynamics and adaptive deep learning for robust EEG motor state decoding.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a compact decoding framework that models gamma burst dynamics via analytic wavelet transform and combines them with spectral features using a multi-stream adaptive deep learning model. It achieves competitive performance in single-channel EEG motor decoding and improves cross-session accuracy by more than 10% over non-adaptive baselines on the WAY-EEG-GAL dataset.

papers.title: Preoperative anxiety, sleep disturbances and postoperative delirium in cardiac surgery: A scoping review for nursing practice.
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesizes evidence from 25 studies (2016-2026) on the relationships between preoperative anxiety, sleep disturbances, and postoperative delirium in cardiac surgery patients. Findings indicate that preoperative anxiety and poor sleep are consistently associated with increased delirium risk, and that psychosocial and sleep-focused nursing interventions may improve perioperative outcomes.

papers.title: Neural regulation in lung cancer: from mechanisms to new therapeutic perspectives.
papers.summary: This review systematically explores the role of the nervous system in lung cancer, focusing on how psychological stress, sleep disorders, and smoking influence tumor initiation and progression via neuroendocrine-immune networks. It details the dual roles of neurotransmitters such as catecholamines, GABA, serotonin, and dopamine in regulating tumor processes and discusses potential therapeutic approaches like β-blockers, while distinguishing clinical evidence from preclinical strategies.

papers.title: [The role of psychosocial risk factors in the development and course of atrial fibrillation].
papers.summary: This scoping review summarizes evidence on psychosocial risk factors for atrial fibrillation (AF), finding consistent associations for depression (15-58% increased risk), insomnia (26-36% increased risk), and work-related stress. It also notes associations with adverse childhood experiences, anxiety, and PTSD, and discusses autonomic, endocrine, and inflammatory mechanisms.

papers.title: Seizure Onset Zone Localization in Drug-Resistant Epilepsy Using Self-Supervised Learning on Stereo-EEG
papers.summary: Developed CSOPE-Net, a self-supervised CNN-Transformer encoder trained on stereo-EEG spectrograms, to localize the seizure onset zone (SOZ) in drug-resistant epilepsy. The model achieved high ROC-AUCs (0.854 cross-validated, 0.935 held-out) and flagged non-SOZ contacts with SOZ-like morphology in poor-outcome patients.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity and Independent Correlates of Cognitive Impairment in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: This study investigated resting-state EEG functional connectivity in atrial fibrillation patients with and without cognitive impairment, finding reduced alpha-band connectivity independently associated with cognitive impairment and a good discriminatory ability for a model combining clinical variables and alpha-band wPLI.

papers.title: Maturation of Sleep EEG Complexity in Preterm Newborns: Insights from Lempel-Ziv and Joint Lempel-Ziv Analyses
papers.summary: This study analyzed EEG from preterm infants using Lempel-Ziv and Joint Lempel-Ziv complexity, finding that complexity differs between sleep states and changes with postmenstrual age, suggesting distinct maturational trajectories for low- and high-frequency EEG activity. These metrics may serve as quantitative biomarkers of neonatal brain maturation.

papers.title: Large Pre-trained EEG Model for Electrical Status Epilepticus during Sleep Detection.
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning framework using a large pre-trained EEG model for automatic detection of electrical status epilepticus during sleep (ESES), incorporating temporal-spatial embeddings and symmetric label smoothing. The method achieved high accuracy (91.91%), sensitivity (91.52%), and specificity (92.37%) on leave-one-subject-out evaluation, outperforming existing approaches.

papers.title: Isolated Adenoidectomy for Pediatric Sleep-Disordered Breathing: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 22 observational studies (4460 children) found isolated adenoidectomy reduced apnea-hypopnea index by mean 11.3 events/h with 75% symptomatic improvement and 17% reoperation rate, supporting its role as a conservative alternative to adenotonsillectomy in selected children.

papers.title: Feasibility of Using Wearables to Monitor Physical Activity and Sleep During Substance Use Disorder Treatment: Insights From a Longitudinal Study.
papers.summary: In a longitudinal study across 8 substance use disorder treatment sites, 20.6% of wearable devices were permanently lost, mostly in residential settings at treatment exit, indicating feasibility requires integrating retrieval into discharge workflows and clarifying responsibility.

papers.title: Elevated delta power in a maternal UBE3A-deletion pig model of Angelman syndrome.
papers.summary: This study found elevated relative delta power in maternal UBE3A-deletion pigs compared to wild-type across vigilance states, particularly during wakefulness, and reduced delta power increase during wake-to-sleep transition. This confirms the pig model reproduces the Angelman syndrome EEG phenotype and supports use of scalp EEG as a translational biomarker.

papers.title: Self-applied single-channel mastoid ExG for fully automated detection of REM sleep behaviour disorder
papers.summary: Developed a fully automated, self-applied system using single-channel mastoid ExG to detect REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD). Achieved AUC 0.95 in home recordings and 0.93 in lab PSG, with automated RWA strongly correlating with expert scoring.

papers.title: Relationship of chronotype, biological rhythm characteristics and sleep quality with suicidal behavior in patients with opioid use disorder.
papers.summary: In 159 opioid use disorder (OUD) patients vs 154 controls, evening chronotype was associated with greater addiction severity, disrupted rhythms, poor sleep quality, and increased suicidality; sleep quality explained a significant portion of the variance between depression and suicidal outcomes.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Resting State Quantitative EEG and Daytime Sleepiness Complaints in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: In Parkinson's disease patients, lower resting-state alpha band (8-10 Hz) phase synchronization within the occipital cortex was the best EEG predictor of higher daytime sleepiness scores (ESS). This suggests disrupted arousal networks may contribute to daytime sleepiness in PD and could serve as a proxy measure.

papers.title: Compared with What? A Missing Comparator for Continuous EEG after Ischemic Stroke.
papers.summary: This letter critiques the lack of a comparator group in studies of continuous EEG after ischemic stroke, arguing that this methodological omission limits interpretation. It highlights the need for appropriate control conditions to draw valid conclusions.

papers.title: Safeguarding Children's Movement Behaviours During Public Health Crises: Lessons From a Global Rapid Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This commentary synthesizes findings from a rapid global scoping review of 182 studies that examined changes in children's movement behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic, finding consistent declines in physical activity and increases in sedentary time. It argues for embedding movement behavior protection in pandemic preparedness and recovery efforts.

papers.title: Antidepressant-Induced Rapid Eye Movement Behavioral Sleep Disorder (RBD): A Scoping Review.
papers.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
papers.summary: This scoping review examined the literature on antidepressant-associated REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), finding that SSRIs, SNRIs, and TCAs are associated with RBD, with a male predominance and depression as common comorbidity. The review included 16 studies and 500 patients, highlighting the need for clinical recognition and monitoring.

papers.title: Sleep duration and sleep problems in non-Hispanic Black adults: a cross-sectional study of the 2015-2020 National Health and Nutritional Examination Survey.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 3,367 non-Hispanic Black adults from the NHANES 2015-2020 found a 53.9% prevalence of recommended sleep duration (7-9h) and 40.5% prevalence of sleep problems. Short sleep was associated with male sex, some college education, working ≥45 hours/week, and history of sleep problems; long sleep with lower education, poverty, unemployment/retirement, and poor health.

papers.title: Reply to "Compared with What? A Missing Comparator for Continuous EEG after Ischemic Stroke".
papers.summary: This letter is a reply to a commentary regarding the use of continuous EEG after ischemic stroke, but the abstract is not provided. The content likely discusses methodological points about comparator groups in EEG studies.

papers.title: Impact of renal impairment, hepatic function, and circadian rhythm on pre-treatment plasma uracil levels.
papers.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
papers.summary: This study of 3,728 patients found that impaired renal function (lower eGFR) is independently associated with elevated plasma uracil levels, with male sex and alkaline phosphatase also positively associated. No circadian variation in plasma uracil was observed.

papers.title: Sleep-Related Problems and Needlestick Injuries Among Nursing Students: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 584 nursing students from two Ecuadorian universities found that 23.6% reported needlestick injuries in the previous three months. Logistic regression showed that younger students and those with insomnia symptoms had higher odds of reporting needlestick injuries.

papers.title: SEEG Contact Detector: A 3D Slicer Extension for Automated Localisation of Intracranial Electrode Contacts
papers.summary: This paper presents an open-source 3D Slicer extension for automated localization of intracranial EEG electrode contacts, achieving a median deviation of 0.10 mm across 78 cases with only 0.65% requiring manual correction. The tool integrates automatic detection and manual correction within a single platform.

papers.title: Metabolic Changes of Perimenopause and Nutritional Advice.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes physiologic metabolic changes during perimenopause and evaluates nutrition and lifestyle interventions that may attenuate adverse metabolic trajectories. It highlights uncertainties regarding the long-term effectiveness of precision nutrition and genotype-informed strategies.

papers.title: Interpretable Topic Modeling of Spontaneous Speech in Depression Using Large Language Models: Multilingual Four-Cohort Study.
papers.summary: This study used large language models to cluster spontaneous speech transcripts from four multilingual cohorts and found that cluster membership was significantly associated with depression severity and diagnoses, with LLM-generated descriptions enhancing interpretability. The 'feelings-and-sleep' question yielded the strongest clinical associations.

papers.title: Association of Social Deprivation with Wait Time and Referral Attrition in Obstructive Sleep Apnea
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 3111 patients referred for obstructive sleep apnea found that higher area-level situational vulnerability was associated with lower odds of scheduling an appointment, while ethnocultural composition was associated with higher odds; no deprivation domain was associated with wait time or missed visits. The findings suggest equity interventions should target referral and scheduling processes.

papers.title: Cross-Sectional Associations of Insomnia, Social Dysfunction, Suicidality, and Depressive Symptoms in Rural Adults with Schizophrenia: A Sex-Stratified Analysis.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 931 rural adults with schizophrenia in China found that insomnia, suicidality, and social dysfunction were associated with depressive symptoms, with no sex differences in these associations. Females had higher scores on all symptom measures, and insomnia showed direct and indirect associations with depression via social dysfunction and suicidality.

papers.title: Cardiac Autonomic Modulation in Seizure Disorders With and Without Interictal Epileptiform Discharges: A Retrospective Heart Rate Variability Analysis Using Archived Digital EEG Recordings.
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared heart rate variability (HRV) parameters among seizure disorder patients with and without interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) and a non-seizure comparison group using ECG from archived EEG recordings. Patients with seizure disorders showed lower vagally mediated HRV (pNN50, total power, HF power) than the comparison group, but no significant HRV differences were found between the two seizure groups, indicating IEDs were not associated with additional autonomic alterations.

papers.title: Association Between Nocturnal Oxygen Desaturation and the Severity of Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 55 OSA patients found that the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) was positively correlated with oxygen desaturation index and T90, and negatively correlated with minimum and mean nocturnal SpO2. The associations were statistically significant, supporting a relationship between OSA severity and nocturnal hypoxemia.

papers.title: Growth of a novel osteopathic manipulative treatment for trauma program integrated into a level 1 trauma center.
papers.summary: This retrospective study evaluated the growth and effectiveness of a novel osteopathic manipulative treatment for trauma (OTP) program integrated into a level 1 trauma center over its first 3 years. The program saw increases in patient volume, RVUs, and referrals, with reduced pain scores and improved mobility reported after treatment.

papers.title: Association of Cleft Phenotype Severity With Childhood Secondary Nasal Intervention Burden and Airway Morbidity Following Primary Cheilorhinoplasty.
papers.summary: This multicenter retrospective study of 1291 patients who underwent primary cheilorhinoplasty found that cleft phenotype severity is independently associated with secondary nasal surgical burden. Patients with bilateral cleft lip and palate had the highest rate and probability of secondary nasal intervention, followed by unilateral cleft lip and palate.

papers.title: Comment on "Self-Reported Sleep Duration, Death-Censored Graft Failure and Health-Related Quality of Life Among Kidney Transplant Recipients: Results From the KNOW-KT Study".
papers.summary: This letter comments on a study about self-reported sleep duration and outcomes in kidney transplant recipients, but the abstract is not provided. It likely discusses methodological or interpretive issues related to the study.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
